name: Cornerstone-Abyss

civilization.name: The Depth Wardens
civilization.notes: Aquatic species inhabiting deep-sea thermal vent cities. Possess metallurgy and basic electrical engineering. No surface presence.

geological_features: Abyssal plains with geometric basalt formations
Mid-ocean ridge spanning the entire equator
specific_features: Deep-sea cities constructed around hydrothermal vents
Metal structures of unknown alloy on the ocean floor
description: Cornerstone-Abyss is a massive oceanic world with a surface area ninety-two percent covered by water. Scattered volcanic island chains provide the only land, their black rock shores battered by heavy swells driven by the planet's strong Coriolis effect. Beneath the surface, the ocean floor is dominated by an equatorial mid-ocean ridge of extraordinary scale, its hydrothermal vent clusters glowing like cities when viewed through deep-sea imaging.

The atmosphere above the ocean is breathable but humid to the point of saturation, with fog banks that can persist for weeks and rainfall that measures in meters per year on the islands. Below the surface, the ocean transitions rapidly from sun-warmed shallows to crushing abyssal depths where the only light comes from bioluminescence and the orange glow of thermal vents. The pressure at the ocean floor exceeds a thousand atmospheres in the deepest trenches.

The Depth Wardens are an aquatic intelligent species that has built a civilization entirely on the ocean floor, centered around the hydrothermal vents that provide heat and energy. Their metallurgy is sophisticated, producing alloys from vent-deposited minerals that resist the extreme pressure and corrosion of their environment. They appear to have no concept of the surface world, their entire cultural and scientific framework oriented downward and inward.

Contact with the Depth Wardens presents unprecedented challenges. They perceive through pressure waves and chemical gradients rather than light, making visual communication impossible. Their industrial activity produces trace exotic matter signatures that have attracted the attention of advanced materials researchers. The ethical framework for engaging with a technologically developing species that is unaware of the universe beyond its ocean is being debated across multiple governing bodies.
